concepts.definition: An enemy going back and forth all the time in its own pattern, without seeing the player.
concepts.example: A guard bat that flies right for 1.5 seconds and left for 1.5 seconds along a corridor.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking a patrol is a single movement block; turning round needs a timer and a reverse.

concepts.definition: The "every N ms" block runs the blocks inside it once every N milliseconds and keeps repeating.
concepts.example: The every 1500 ms block turns the bat round every one and a half seconds.
concepts.pitfall: Thinking 1000 ms is 1000 seconds; 1000 ms is only 1 second.

concepts.definition: Speed is the number of pixels travelled each second; distance = speed x time.
concepts.example: If the speed is 40 and the time is 1.5 seconds, the bat travels 60 pixels.
concepts.pitfall: Leaving the time in milliseconds when you calculate: multiplying by 1500 ms gives a very different answer from multiplying by 1.5 seconds.

concepts.definition: Changes the sign of the speed on the chosen axis: 40 becomes -40, and -40 becomes 40.
concepts.example: When a bat with an x speed of 40 is reversed, it goes left at 40 pixels/s.
concepts.pitfall: Leaving y (up-down) selected in the block; the sideways speed never changes and the bat does not turn.

concepts.definition: A label given to a sprite; rules are written for the sprite's kind.
concepts.example: Because the bat is of the Enemy kind, a collision rule written later will apply to the bat too.
concepts.pitfall: Choosing the wrong kind: the rule cannot find the kind it expects and never runs.

quiz.prompt: The bat's sideways speed is 50 pixels/s. A timer reverses the speed every 2000 ms. How many pixels does the bat travel in one direction before it turns?
quiz.explanation: 2000 ms = 2 seconds. Distance = speed x time = 50 x 2 = 100 pixels. Multiplying by the time in milliseconds (2000) would give 100000; change it to seconds before you calculate.

quiz.prompt: You put a "set yarasa speed x 40, y 0" block inside the bat's timer. The bat does not turn; it keeps going right. Why?
options: The timer must be at least 50 ms
The bat cannot turn because it is of the Enemy kind
Speed blocks do not work inside a timer
Every time it runs, the speed is set to 40 again; there is no block that changes the sign of the speed
quiz.explanation: The speed block sets the speed to the given value; it does not reverse it. 40 is written as 40 again and again. To turn, you need the "reverse" block, which changes the sign of the speed. The 50 ms timer limit is not the problem here, and the kind does not stop it turning either.

quiz.prompt:
The bat starts at x = 50. The program is:

```
when game starts:
  set yarasa speed x 30, y 0

every 1000 ms:
  reverse yarasa x speed
```

After 3.5 seconds, where is the bat and which way is it going?
options: At about x = 155, off the screen
quiz.explanation: 0-1 s right: x = 80. 1-2 s left: x = 50. 2-3 s right: x = 80. At 3 seconds the third reverse makes the speed -30; in 0.5 seconds it goes 15 pixels left, so x = 65. So it is at about 65 and going left.

quiz.prompt:
The bat goes right but never comes back. Which is the bug?

```
when game starts:
  set yarasa speed x 40, y 0

every 1500 ms:
  reverse yarasa y (up-down) speed
```
options: The starting speed should not be 40
The timer should not be 1500 ms
y (up-down) is selected in the reverse block; the sideways speed does not change
The bat's kind label is missing
quiz.explanation: The bat moves sideways, but the reverse is applied to the up-down speed. The up-down speed is already 0, so reversing it changes nothing; the sideways speed never changes. The fix: set the axis in the block to x (sideways). The other lines have no bug.

quiz.prompt: The bat's timer is 800 ms. The times going and coming back are equal. Every how many milliseconds does the bat come back to its starting point?
quiz.explanation: Every 800 ms the speed is reversed: it goes 800 ms one way and 800 ms the other way. A full round trip takes 800 + 800 = 1600 ms, and the bat is back at its starting point.
